title: Assessment of osteoporosis knowledge in patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases using the German version of the OKAT – a non-interventional cross-sectional study
summary:
This study aims to assess how much patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases know about osteoporosis. Osteoporosis is a condition in which bones become less stable and are more likely to break. Patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases have an increased risk of osteoporosis and fractures, and treatment with glucocorticoids such as prednisolone may further increase this risk.

Participants will complete a short questionnaire once. The study uses the German version of the Osteoporosis Knowledge Assessment Test (OKAT), which measures knowledge about osteoporosis risk factors, prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. A few additional questions will ask about age, sex, rheumatic diagnosis, known osteoporosis, current prednisolone/cortisone use, calcium or vitamin D supplementation, and whether the participant has previously received medical advice on osteoporosis prevention.

The study is non-interventional and anonymous. No additional examinations, medical procedures, or treatment changes will be performed. Completing the questionnaire takes approximately 5–10 minutes. The results should help identify knowledge gaps and support the development of better patient information and prevention strategies for people with inflammatory rheumatic diseases.
conditions: Systemic lupus erythematosus with organ or system involvement

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patient with an  inflammatory rheumatic disease, or patient with osteoporosis without an inflammatory rheumatic disease 
- Sufficient German language skills to complete the questionnaire independently 
- Consent to participate
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of capacity to provide consent 
- Incomplete OKAT 
- Repeated participation
